Input $0<\alpha<1$, a step size $h>0$, an integer $N\ge1$, $\lambda\ge0$,
an initial value $u_0$, and forcing values $F^1,\ldots,F^N$. If any
admissibility condition fails, return `invalid-input`. Set $\omega_0=1$ and
compute $\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_N$ in increasing order by

$$\omega_j:=\frac{j-1-\alpha}{j}\,\omega_{j-1}.$$

Set $V^0=0$ and $U^0=u_0$. For $n=1,\ldots,N$ in increasing order, compute

$$V^n:=\frac{F^n-\lambda u_0-h^{-\alpha}\sum_{j=1}^n\omega_jV^{n-j}}{h^{-\alpha}+\lambda},\qquad U^n:=u_0+V^n.$$

For any sequence $V^0,\ldots,V^N$ with $V^0=0$, use the notation

$$\bar\partial_h^\alpha V^n:=h^{-\alpha}\sum_{j=0}^n\omega_jV^{n-j}.$$

Return $U^0,\ldots,U^N$. A finite-precision implementation that cannot
certify a scalar solve returns `solve-failed` without reporting a value. No
FFT or truncated-memory error claim is included.

Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^{2d}$ be open and $H\in C^2(U)$. Write $z=(q,p)$ in canonical coordinates, set $J=\begin{pmatrix}0&I\\-I&0\end{pmatrix}$, and define the finite-regularity coordinate field
$$F(q,p):=\bigl(\nabla_pH(q,p),-\nabla_qH(q,p)\bigr)=J\nabla H(q,p).$$
Given $z\in U$, for a signed step $h$, the **exact local implicit midpoint step** is defined by
$$Z=z+\frac h2F(Z),\qquad z^+=2Z-z,$$
using the locally unique solution $Z$ in a declared closed ball $\overline B(z,\rho)\subset U$. The branch is admissible when certified bounds $M\ge\sup_{\overline B}\|F\|$ and $L\ge\sup_{\overline B}\|DF\|$ satisfy $|h|M/2\le\rho$ and $|h|L/2<1$. It returns `branch-not-certified` if the ball or bounds are unavailable, and `domain-failure` if the admitted ball is not contained in $U$.

For a finite iteration implementation of these exact operations, input an output tolerance $\tau>0$ and an update budget $B\in\mathbb N_0$. Use $\theta=|h|L/2$ and proceed as follows.

1. Set $Z_0=z$. If $B=0$, return `inconclusive` with current stage iterate $Z_0$, approximate output $z$, and output-error bound $2\rho$.
2. If $B\ge1$, compute $Z_1=z+(h/2)F(Z_0)$ and set $d_1=\|Z_1-Z_0\|$.

Otherwise, if $k<B$, compute $Z_{k+1}=z+(h/2)F(Z_k)$ and continue. If the check fails at $k=B$, return `inconclusive` with current stage iterate $Z_B$, approximate output $2Z_B-z$, and output-error bound $2b_B$.

Input real numbers $a<b$, a natural $n\ge0$, sampled values $y_0,\ldots,y_n$, and the phase/FFT controls for [[alg-na-computed-fast-transforms-and-convolution]]: a phase tolerance $0<\tau\le1/4$, integer dyadic exponent limits $e_{\min}\le e_{\max}$, an initial phase precision $p_0\ge2$, a finite precision cap $p_{\max}\ge p_0$, a finite elementary-series cap $J\ge1$, and a maximum radix-two recursion depth $d_{\max}\ge0$. Set $m=(a+b)/2$ and $d=(b-a)/2$. For an underlying $f\in C[a,b]$, admissible samples satisfy $y_0=f(m)$ when $n=0$ and $y_j=f(m+d\cos(j\pi/n))$ for $0\le j\le n$ when $n\ge1$, using the canonical real images of [[def-canonical-natural]]. The output is an approximate real quadrature value or the first status returned by the called DFT procedure.

1. If $n=0$, return $(b-a)y_0$, the midpoint convention of [[def-na-clenshaw-curtis-quadrature]].
2. If $n\ge1$, form $z\in\mathbb C^{2n}$ by $z_j:=y_j+0i$ for $0\le j\le n$ and $z_{2n-j}:=y_j+0i$ for $1\le j<n$. This is the even extension $(y_0,\ldots,y_n,y_{n-1},\ldots,y_1)$, with real samples embedded as complex numbers with zero imaginary part. Call [[alg-na-computed-fast-transforms-and-convolution]] on $z$ with length $2n$ and the same controls $(\tau,e_{\min},e_{\max},p_0,p_{\max},J,d_{\max})$. If it returns a status instead of a vector, return that status.
3. Otherwise, take the real parts $X_k$ of output entries $0\le k\le n$, form the DCT-I coefficients $a_0=X_0/(2n)$, $a_n=X_n/(2n)$, and $a_k=X_k/n$ for $1\le k<n$ as in [[def-na-clenshaw-curtis-dct-i]], and return $d\sum_{k=0}^n a_k\mu_k$ with the exact moments $\mu_k$ in [[def-na-clenshaw-curtis-quadrature]].

The postprocessing is exact real arithmetic applied to the approximate DFT output. The procedure makes no end-to-end floating-point error or stability claim; it only propagates the DFT routine's declared failure statuses.

Input a real function $f$ on a nondegenerate closed interval $[a,b]$ and an integer $L\ge0$. The output is the finite triangular table $(R_{\ell,j})_{0\le j\le\ell\le L}$ and its top entry $R_{L,L}$.

1. For each $\ell=0,\ldots,L$, set $N_\ell:=2^\ell\in\mathbb N$ using natural exponentiation of [[def-nat-power]], $h_\ell:=(b-a)/N_\ell$, and $R_{\ell,0}:=T_{N_\ell}(f)$ using the composite trapezoidal value $T_N$ of [[def-composite-trapezoidal-rule]]. Natural powers in real scalar expressions are understood through their canonical real images.
2. For $j=1,\ldots,L$, and then for each $\ell=j,\ldots,L$, set
$$R_{\ell,j}:=R_{\ell,j-1}+\frac{R_{\ell,j-1}-R_{\ell-1,j-1}}{4^j-1}.$$

For $j\ge1$, claim 3 of [[lem-power-monotone]] gives $4^j\ge4>1$, using the natural-to-real power identity of [[def-nat-power]]; thus every displayed denominator $4^j-1$ is the positive real $4^j-1$ and is invertible by [[thm-reals-field]]. This definition returns only the stated finite table; it makes no accuracy claim for nonsmooth inputs or finite-precision arithmetic.

anchor.description: the positive-order integral formula and strict Caputo-order domain
anchor.quote:
Let $T>0$ and $\beta>0$. For $g\in L^1(0,T)$, its left fractional
integral of order $\beta$ is, for almost every $t\in(0,T)$,

$$I^\beta g(t):=\frac{1}{\Gamma(\beta)}\int_0^t(t-s)^{\beta-1}g(s)\,ds.$$

The definition uses Lebesgue integration, with
[[def-indefinite-lebesgue-integral-on-a-compact-interval]] and
[[def-l-one-of-a-measure]]. The kernel is integrable and
$$\int_0^t(t-s)^{\beta-1}\,ds=\frac{t^\beta}{\beta}$$
by [[lem-fractional-integral-kernel-power-integral]]. Tonelli's theorem
[[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] therefore gives
$$\int_0^T\int_0^t(t-s)^{\beta-1}|g(s)|\,ds\,dt =\int_0^T|g(s)|\int_s^T(t-s)^{\beta-1}dt\,ds \le \frac{T^\beta}{\beta}\|g\|_{L^1(0,T)}<\infty,$$
so the defining integral is finite for almost every $t$. For continuous $g$,
it is finite at every $t\in[0,T]$ and
$$|I^\beta g(t)|\le \frac{t^\beta}{\beta\Gamma(\beta)}\|g\|_\infty =\frac{t^\beta}{\Gamma(\beta+1)}\|g\|_\infty,$$
using [[thm-real-gamma-functional-equation]].

For $0<\alpha<1$ and an absolutely continuous function
$u:[0,T]\to\mathbb R$ whose almost-everywhere derivative belongs to
$L^1(0,T)$, its Caputo derivative of order $\alpha$ is the
almost-everywhere defined function

$$D_C^\alpha u:=I^{1-\alpha}u'=\frac{1}{\Gamma(1-\alpha)}\int_0^t(t-s)^{-\alpha}u'(s)\,ds.$$

Here absolute continuity is as in
[[def-absolutely-continuous-function]]. Under Countable Choice
([[def-countable-choice]]), every such absolutely continuous $u$ has
$u'\in L^1(0,T)$ by
[[thm-absolutely-continuous-functions-have-integrable-derivatives]], so the
Caputo derivative is defined on the whole absolutely continuous class under
that assumption. Without Countable Choice, the same formula is defined for
each absolutely continuous $u$ whose derivative is separately known to be in
$L^1(0,T)$. The Gamma factors are the positive real Euler Gamma function
[[def-real-gamma-function-by-the-euler-integral]].

anchor.quote:
Let $a<b$, let $x_1,\ldots,x_s\in[a,b]$ be a finite indexed list (repetitions are allowed), and let $w_1,\ldots,w_s\in\mathbb R$. For every Riemann-integrable $f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$, define the quadrature value and residual by
$$Q(f):=\sum_{i=1}^{s}w_i f(x_i),\qquad L(f):=\int_a^b f(x)\,dx-Q(f).$$
For a natural $r\ge1$, say that $Q$ is exact through degree $r-1$ if $L(p)=0$ for every formal real polynomial $p$ of degree at most $r-1$ ([[def-real-polynomial-degree-leading-coefficient-and-monic]]). Here $r-1$ is the natural predecessor specified by [[def-factorial-and-falling-factorial]]. For any natural $q$, the factorial $q!$ in a real-valued formula denotes its canonical real image under [[def-canonical-natural]]. This denominator is nonzero: $q!\ne0$ by [[def-factorial-and-falling-factorial]], every nonzero natural is a successor by [[lem-nat-nonzero-is-successor]] and therefore is at least $1$ in the natural order [[def-nat-order]], and its canonical real image is positive by [[lem-of-naturals-positive]], hence invertible by [[thm-reals-field]]. For $t\in[a,b]$ define
$$g_{r,t}(x):=\begin{cases}\dfrac{(x-t)^{r-1}}{(r-1)!},&x>t,\\0,&x\le t,\end{cases}\qquad K_r(t):=L(g_{r,t}).$$
The power is the natural power of [[def-integer-power]]. For $r\ge2$, $g_{r,t}$ is polynomial and continuous on each side of $t$ by [[thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions]]; the polynomial branch extends to $t$ with value $0$ because $r-1\ge1$, agreeing with the zero branch. Thus it is continuous on $[a,b]$ and Riemann-integrable by [[thm-continuous-implies-integrable]]. For $r=1$ it is the indicator of $(t,b]$; if $t=b$ it is zero, and if $t<b$, for each $\varepsilon>0$ choose $s\in(t,b)$ with $s-t<\varepsilon$ and use the partition with breakpoints $a,t,s,b$ after deleting repeated endpoints. The indicator is constant on all panels except $[t,s]$, where its oscillation is $1$, so its upper-minus-lower sum is at most $s-t<\varepsilon$; [[thm-riemann-criterion]] makes it integrable. At $r=1$ the denominator is $0!=1$. Once $K_1$ is shown integrable, changing its values at the finitely many quadrature nodes does not change its integral by [[lem-changing-a-function-at-finitely-many-points]].

triple. Let $a(t;\cdot,\cdot):V_h\times V_h\to\mathbb R$ be real bilinear

$E\subset(0,T)$ outside which, with common constants $0\le M<\infty$ and
$\alpha>0$,
$$|a(t;v_h,w_h)|\le M\|v_h\|_V\|w_h\|_V,\qquad a(t;v_h,v_h)\ge\alpha\|v_h\|_V^2\qquad(v_h,w_h\in V_h).$$

$u_h\in H^1(0,T;V_h)$ be the semidiscrete solution from
[[thm-parabolic-finite-dimensional-measurable-ode]]. On a finite partition

$\tau_{\max}=\max_j\tau_j$. For the interval-averaged backward Euler values
$U^j$ from [[alg-parabolic-backward-euler-averaged-forms]], define
$e^j=U^j-u_h(t_j)$ and let $\widehat U$ be the affine reconstruction, with
$\overline U(t)=U^j$ on $(t_{j-1},t_j)$. Every step has a unique solution.
With
$$C_U=\|U^0\|_H^2+\alpha^{-1}\|f\|_{L^2(0,T;V_h^*)}^2,$$
the separate maximum and cumulative bounds are
$$\max_{0\le m\le N}\|U^m\|_H^2\le C_U,\qquad \sum_{j=1}^N\|U^j-U^{j-1}\|_H^2+ \alpha\sum_{j=1}^N\tau_j\|U^j\|_V^2\le C_U.$$

$$\|\widehat U'\|_{L^2(0,T;V_h^*)}^2 \le2\|f\|_{L^2(V_h^*)}^2+2M^2\|\overline U\|_{L^2(V)}^2,$$
$$\|\widehat U-\overline U\|_{L^2(0,T;V_h^*)}^2 \le\frac{c_i^2\tau_{\max}}3 \sum_{j=1}^N\|U^j-U^{j-1}\|_H^2,$$
where $c_i=\|V\hookrightarrow H\|$. For the nodal error, define
$$C_e=\|e^0\|_H^2+ \frac{M^2}{\alpha}\tau_{\max}^2 \|u_h'\|_{L^2(0,T;V_h)}^2.$$
Then the error obeys the separate bounds
$$\max_{0\le m\le N}\|e^m\|_H^2\le C_e,\qquad \alpha\sum_{j=1}^N\tau_j\|e^j\|_V^2\le C_e.$$
Thus exact initial projection $U^0=u_h(0)$ gives first-order maximum nodal
error. The reconstruction estimates provide bounds for later compactness
arguments; they do not themselves assert compactness.

Assume Countable Choice and the bounded polyhedral mesh setting, spaces,
form and data of [[thm-parabolic-fem-semidiscrete-existence-energy]]. Let $u$
be the continuous solution supplied by
[[thm-parabolic-variational-wellposedness-and-energy-stability]] on the same
evolution triple and let $u_h$ be the corresponding semidiscrete solution.
For this error identity, assume the additional regularity $u\in H^1(0,T;V)$,
meaning $u,u'\in L^2(0,T;V)$ with the unique continuous representative
supplied by [[lem-parabolic-projection-time-product-rule]]. Let
$P_h:V\to V_h$ be a fixed bounded linear
comparison map, define
$$\rho(t)=P_hu(t)-u(t),\qquad\theta(t)=u_h(t)-P_hu(t),$$
and let $\mathcal R_h(t)\in V_h^*$ be the full residual
$$\mathcal R_h(t)(v_h)=(\rho'(t),v_h)_H+a(t;\rho(t),v_h).$$
Then for almost every $t$ and every $v_h\in V_h$,
$$(\theta'(t),v_h)_H+a(t;\theta(t),v_h)=-\mathcal R_h(t)(v_h),$$
and for every $t\in[0,T]$,
$$\|\theta(t)\|_H^2+\alpha\int_0^t\|\theta(s)\|_V^2ds \le\|\theta(0)\|_H^2+ \alpha^{-1}\int_0^t\|\mathcal R_h(s)\|_{V_h^*}^2ds.$$

The same identity and energy bound hold for an operator-norm $C^1$
time-dependent comparison map $P_h(t):V\to V_h$, with its time derivative
included in $\rho'$ as stated below. For a time-independent form and the
Ritz projection $P_h=R_h$ from
[[def-parabolic-ritz-projection]], Galerkin orthogonality makes
$a(\rho(t),v_h)=0$, so the residual is exactly
$(R_hu'(t)-u'(t),v_h)_H$. If a time-dependent comparison $P_h(t)$ is used,
it must be operator-norm $C^1$; then
$\rho'=P_h'(t)u+P_h(t)u'-u'$, including the projection-derivative term.
For a measurable time-dependent form with a fixed comparison map, no
orthogonality is inferred and the full displayed residual remains.

anchor.description: the real separable Hilbert evolution setting, which permits the scalar triple
anchor.quote:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $T>0$, let $V$ be a separable real Hilbert
space, and let $(V,H,V^*)$ be its real evolution triple. Suppose
$a(t;\cdot,\cdot):V\times V\to\mathbb R$ is bilinear and scalar measurable
for each fixed pair $v,w\in V$, and there is one null set outside which
$$|a(t;v,w)|\le M\|v\|_V\|w\|_V,\qquad a(t;v,v)\ge\alpha\|v\|_V^2$$
for all $v,w\in V$, with constants $M>0$ and $\alpha>0$. Let
$f\in L^2(0,T;V^*)$ and $u_0\in H$. Then there is a unique
$u\in W(0,T;V)$ with $u(0)=u_0$ and, for almost every $t$,
$$\langle u'(t),v\rangle_{V^*,V}+a(t;u(t),v) =\langle f(t),v\rangle_{V^*,V}\qquad(v\in V).$$
For every $t\in[0,T]$ it satisfies
$$\|u(t)\|_H^2+\alpha\int_0^t\|u(s)\|_V^2\,ds \le\|u_0\|_H^2+\alpha^{-1}\int_0^t\|f(s)\|_{V^*}^2\,ds.$$
The proof applies BNB to the space-time form. Scalar measurability suffices
because $V$ is separable and the measurable inverse action is proved locally.
